body.x: Sheco Co., Ltd. (CEO Kwon Ki-sung) participated in CES 2024 in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th.

Sheco uses drones to present a solution for purifying various pollutants in marine and water areas. The company’s self-developed water quality purification drone, ‘Sheco Ark-M,’ is a product that automates the cleaning of contaminants on the water’s surface, traditionally performed manually by ship crew members.

Various industrial pollutants such as oil, wastewater, cargo dust, and harmful algae blooms occur in different environments. Separate facilities, equipment, personnel, and processes are operated to handle each type of pollutant, incurring costs and time. In contrast, Sheco Ark, with its all-in-one design, offers versatility for various contaminants, providing economic efficiency in water quality purification and contributing to national-scale water resource management.

Additionally, Sheco aims to achieve complete autonomy and data disclosure in the overall water quality management system, including surface water pollutant purification drones, AI pollutant recognition cameras, and data collection. The company continuously develops environmentally friendly technologies, aiming to apply clean technology to marine environments, similar to robotic vacuum cleaners inside homes.

A Sheco representative mentioned, “Currently, in Korea, oil spill marine accidents occur approximately 256 times a year, almost every other day. Globally, various water pollution issues are arising, each requiring different experts, personnel, equipment, and processes for handling.” Sheco has addressed these challenges by developing wireless small-scale unified equipment, allowing non-experts to respond immediately to pollution incidents with just 30 minutes of training.

Moreover, Sheco Ark’s purification service differs from conventional pollutant recovery and treatment methods—the traditional way involved absorbing pollutants and water, requiring a cumbersome secondary separation process. In contrast, Sheco Ark developed technology for ‘real-time pollutant separation,’ simultaneously suctioning and separating contaminants and moisture. The separated pollutants are stored in cartridges, while purified water is immediately discharged.

The Sheco representative emphasized, “Sheco Ark is a product that automates water quality management in marine and water areas, a task that previously required ships and personnel. With about 30 minutes of training, even a non-expert can use it immediately. In addition to the product’s automatic solution, our in-house-developed electromagnetic sediment recovery system enables the complete automation of the entire work process without needing personnel.”

Furthermore, “The automation of the work process ensures freedom from health issues such as respiratory, joint, and nervous system diseases caused by contact with pollutants during conventional work. The Sheco Ark does not require additional facilities, ships, heavy equipment, or specialized skills for pollutant recovery. It makes introducing it easy, even when investment in water quality management is challenging, such as small and medium-sized enterprises and developing countries.”

body.cap: A featured article on Ubergizmo covering the CES exhibition was reported through a media interview with Ubergizmo, a U.S.-based media outlet.

body.x: Regarding its participation in CES 2024, Sheco received innovation awards in two categories (Drones and unmanned Systems and Products supporting Human Security). The company sees this as a starting point for entering the North American market, which holds over 40% of the marine pollution control market, with many existing devices entering the market. Sheco plans to conduct one proof-of-concept project for water pollution incidents in the North American region in 2024, aiming for international joint development projects to enhance the product and establish a fully autonomous pollution control system.
